nodes.name: Ball-milling and Calcination of Ternary RuO2
nodes.procedure: The co-doped RuO2 catalysts were synthesized through a scalable method suitable for industrial production. In brief, a homogeneous mixture of sodium chloride and metal precursors (Cr, Sn, Ru precursors) was prepared via ball-milling, followed by calcination.
nodes.source_text: The co-doped RuO₂ catalysts were synthesized through a salable method suitable for industrial production. In brief, a homogeneous mixture of sodium chloride and metal precursors was prepared via ball-milling, followed by calcination (see details of the synthesis approach).

nodes.description: Acidic OER performance in 0.5 M H2SO4 three-electrode system (all catalysts)
nodes.source_text: the Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 displayed the highest acidic OER catalytic activity, with an overpotential of 178 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm^{-2} ... Tafel analysis revealing a small slope of 47.3 mV decade^{-1}

The current-voltage curve of the Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2-based cell reached a nominal current density of 3.0 A cm^{-2} at just 1.77 V under industrial operational settings (80°C) ... After elevating the operation current density as large as 15 A cm^{-2}, the cell delivered a consistently low cell voltage of 2.4 V

nodes.description: PEMWE stability at 500 mA/cm² and 1000 mA/cm² for 1000h and 500h
nodes.source_text: The Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 showed a negligible increase in cell voltage when operating at the current densities of 500 and 1000 mA cm^{-2} for at least 1000 and 500 h correspondingly
In single-cell configurations with a 100 cm² active area, we achieved a current exceeding 300 A at a cell voltage below 3.0 V ... the five-cell stack operated at a total voltage of 9.0 V (1.8 V/cell)

nodes.description: Acidic OER stability chronopotentiometry at 10 mA/cm²
nodes.source_text: chronopotentiometric testing at 10 mA cm^{-2} over 100 h, outperforming the RuO_2-C
The outstanding robustness of the Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 was further proved by 1000 cyclic voltammetry (CV) cycles without any obvious activity changes

nodes.characterization_summary: Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 reveals typical nanoparticle morphology with average diameter of ~10 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images (Figures S3, S4), Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 revealed a typical nanoparticle morphology with an average diameter of ∼10 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images show typical nanoparticle morphology with average diameter of ~10 nm for Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2; SAED pattern demonstrates polycrystalline structure with distinct diffraction rings.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images (Figures S3, S4), Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 revealed a typical nanoparticle morphology with an average diameter of ∼10 nm. The corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern demonstrated the polycrystalline structure of the Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 with distinct diffraction rings (Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms phase-pure rutile RuO_2 architecture for Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 after metal doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Crystallographic analysis via X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns confirms phase-pure rutile RuO_2 architecture after doping of those metals (Figure S8).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show characteristic RuO_2 vibrational fingerprints at 498, 617, and 684 cm^{-1} (E_g, A_{1g}, B_{2g}); B_{2g} peak intensity decreases after Sn and Cr doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Complementary structural insights from Raman spectra reveal characteristic vibrational fingerprints at 498, 617, and 684 cm^{-1} attributed to the E_g, A_{1g}, and B_{2g}, respectively... After Sn and Cr introduced, the intensity of the B_{2g} peak decreased in Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows lattice fringe spacings of 0.169, 0.256, and 0.318 nm assigned to (211), (101), and (110) planes of rutile RuO_2; atomic strengths of Sn, Cr, and Ru clearly distinguished.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscope (HAADF-STEM) image of the Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 demonstrates the lattice fringe spacings of 0.169, 0.256, and 0.318 nm assigned to the (211), (101), and (110) planes of rutile RuO_2... the intensity profile along the rectangles offers compelling proof that the atomic strengths of Sn, Cr, and Ru species could be clearly distinguished.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS measures Cr and Sn contents in Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 as 4.9 wt.% and 12.8 wt.% respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contents of Cr and Sn in the Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 are measured by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) to be 4.9 and 12.8 wt.% respectively (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping demonstrates homogenous distribution of Ru, Sn, Cr, and O elements throughout Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping images demonstrate the homogenous distribution of Ru, Sn, Cr, and O elements throughout the Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p_{3/2} XPS peaks at 462.0 eV (Ru^{4+}) and 464.4 eV (Ru^{>4+}); Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 shows highest Ru^{>4+} proportion of 41.85%; Cr 2p peaks at 575.1 eV (Cr(III)), 576.1 eV (Cr(IV)), 578.0 eV (CrO_2H); Sn 3d_{3/2} peak shifts negatively confirming electron withdrawing effect of Sn(IV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the XPS spectra of Ru 3p_{3/2} of the as-prepared samples could be deconvoluted into two peaks located at about 462.0 and 464.4 eV, attributed to the Ru^{4+} 3p_{3/2} and Ru^{>4+} 3p_{3/2} respectively... the proportion of Ru^{>4+} in the Sn-doped samples was increased and reached the highest value of 41.85% for the best performing Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2... For Cr XPS 2p spectra, three peaks could be observed on Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2... located at about 575.1, 576.1 and 578.0 eV, which are assigned to Cr (III), Cr (IV), CrO_2H, respectively... The binding energy of Sn 3d_{3/2} peak shifted negatively after introduced into the RuO_2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows absorption edge shift to higher energy for Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 indicating increased Ru valence; Sn K-edge shows lower near-edge absorption energy; shorter Ru-O bonding length and reduced coordination number (5.6) vs RuO_2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ru K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra... the absorption edge of Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 was found to be slightly shifted to higher energy compared with that of RuO_2... a slightly reduced distance of Ru-O bonding was discerned for Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2... The model-based fitting results revealed shorter Ru-O bonds and a reduced Ru-O coordination number (5.6 and 5.9, respectively) compared to RuO_2.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Cr-OH stretching band at 796 cm^{-1} exclusively in Cr-doped samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy was further employed... The broad feature at 796 cm^{-1}, attributed to symmetric and anti-symmetric Cr-OH stretching, was exclusively observed in Cr-doped samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS at 1.42 V shows Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 has the lowest charge transfer resistance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) of the Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 at 1.42 V showed the lowest charge transfer resistance (Figure S15).

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA of Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 is 31.2 mF cm^{-2}, 8.2 times higher than RuO_2-C (3.8 mF cm^{-2}).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) of the Cr_{0.1}Sn_{0.1}Ru_{0.8}O_2 determined to be 31.2 mF cm^{-2} (Figure S16), nearly 8.2 times higher than the RuO_2-C (3.8 mF cm^{-2}).
